script: I was deceived not only by someone I was dating, but also by his friend.. I had been seeing a guy for about four months. We were both international students, both gay, both craving connection. He had this easy charm that made me feel like we were the only two people in the world. We started out as roommates in a tiny apartment on campus, and then the line between roommate and boyfriend blurred. He'd text me early in the morning, saying, "Hey, coffee?" and I'd reply, "Sure, love." We'd end the day in his kitchen, laughing at memes, and that's when I felt safe. But here's the thing… The first time I noticed something off was when I saw a text from him to a number that wasn't his. He was on a call with someone, and I could hear him saying his ex's name. What I didn't know was that his ex was still in his life like a ghost haunting the walls of his apartment. They'd still be in contact, exchanging emails about school projects, and sometimes he'd call his ex to vent. It was like watching a movie where the villain keeps coming back. I tried to brush it off, thinking maybe he just needed a friend. However, the stakes were higher than a casual friendship. If he was still connected to his ex, he could be leaking my secrets. I kept finding out these details after the fact, like a detective catching clues at midnight. I didn't ask him to cut ties; I just wanted transparency. When he finally told me that he had a "friend" from home staying with him, I thought I was in the clear. But here's the thing… The "friend" was actually his ex, disguised as a female with a different name. He'd been pretending to be a girl, telling me he was hosting two "female friends." And that's when everything changed. I was sitting in his living room, scrolling through my phone, when I saw a photo of a guy with a beard, the same face I'd seen on his social media. The picture was a bomb. I felt my stomach drop to the floor, like watching a car crash in slow motion. My heart was pounding, and my brain was screaming, "What the—?" I called him immediately. He answered, "Hey, what's up?" I told him I saw the photo, and he paused like he was waiting for a punchline. He said, "I didn't do it to hurt you." And that was the first time he tried to justify the lie. What I didn't know was that the other "female friend" was also part of the deception. She'd never met me before, but she had sat with him and laughed while he told me the story. I felt my confidence wobble like a tower of Jenga. I was like, "Are you trying to make me feel like a fool?" But here's the thing… He said, "You wouldn't have found out if you hadn't looked." He was basically blaming me for the curiosity that led to the truth. I was losing my mind. If I didn't confront him, the lie would stay buried, and I'd live in a fake reality. The stakes were insane. This wasn't just about a guy pretending to be a girl; it was about trust, about my heart, about my sense of self. I wanted to know why he didn't tell me earlier. He said, "I didn't want to hurt you." His words felt like a broken record, repeating a lie that had no weight. But here's the thing… I had been thinking about what it meant to be in a relationship with someone who could keep secrets that made me feel invisible. The next day, I walked into his apartment with the photo in my hand. He looked at me and said, "Why did you do that?" He was deflecting, like a bad magician. I could feel my anger rising, but I also felt a hollow spot where trust used to be. I asked him if he could explain why he chose to lie. He said, "Nothing happened, so what's the problem?" I wanted to know what he was really hiding. He said he didn't consider it betrayal, just a mistake. I said it was betrayal. He treated my feelings like a side issue, like a small problem. It was like he was saying, "You're reading too much into this." I felt like I was drowning in a sea of lies. My body remembered the closeness; my mind kept replaying the betrayal. I ended it. I blocked him on every platform, and I felt relief, like a breath of fresh air. But the sadness stayed, a heavy stone in my chest. And here's the thing… I still miss the moments we shared, the late-night chats, the way he would hold my hand. It was like a love story that ended mid‑sentence. I started to wonder if the lie was the real problem, or if it was the way he handled it. If he had been honest, would I have stayed? If I had been more demanding, would he have listened? The truth is, I was hurt not just by the deception, but by the lack of genuine remorse. He didn't apologize; he deflected. It was a cold, hard realization that someone I loved was also a liar. But here's the thing… The next time I looked at my phone, I saw a notification from the friend who had been part of the lie. She was sending me a text saying, "We're still friends." I realized that my heart had been playing a game with strangers who knew my secrets. I was left feeling like a character in someone else's plot. The stakes were personal. I risked my mental health, my sense of self, my future happiness. If I didn't confront it, the lie would stay buried. I needed to find closure, not just for me but for the people who were in my life. If I didn't do that, the betrayal would haunt me forever. But here's the thing… I was not ready to let go. I was ready to fight for the truth. And that's when everything changed…
